transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-26
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Rivera (Redwood SE), Aisha Thompson (VioletMesh Head of ML), Ben Ko (VioletMesh Platform Eng), Sam Ortega (VioletMesh Product)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style health check + fast-track pilot gating. Focus: current usage signals, resilience/latency concerns during peak, and what Redwood needs to accelerate their pilot to production (SOC2/benchmarks/pricing).

Topics discussed:
- Current traffic and burst profile
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs (dedicated vs hosted)
- Security & compliance gating (SOC2, SSO, KMS)
- Benchmarking plan & telemetry needed
- Next steps to enable pilot acceleration

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, we'll start the sync. I'm Maya from Redwood, Diego's with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Aisha: Good thanks, running between meetings but we wanted to get this across the finish line this week.
[00:09] Ben: Yeah quick call, we have some spikes this week so perfect timing.
[00:12] Maya: Great. Objective is simple — figure out what we need to unblock a production-like pilot. Diego will cover the benchmark plan, I'll cover pricing and pilot terms, and then we can triage any security asks.
[00:24] Diego: Cool. Quick reminder on what we've seen so far from the trial logs: your median P95 token latency on hosted small models was ~240ms but there are tail spikes up to 900ms during 2x burst windows — looks like those align with nightly batch jobs plus some user-initiated heavy requests.
[00:40] Sam: Yeah those nights are exactly when we run extraction and a bunch of embeddings for the search index, plus a new feature that batches many calls.
[00:48] Ben: To add, our peak concurrency can move from 50 to 1,200 requests in 10 minutes — so there's a slope there that worries us.
[00:56] Diego: That's a big factor. For that profile we usually recommend Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or hosted with a burst plan if you want to avoid ops overhead. The trade is cost predictability vs operational ownership.
[01:08] Aisha: We're trying to avoid onboarding a whole infra team to run infra. Can Redwood Dedicated meet our latency SLOs? We target 200ms P95 for interactive routes.
[01:18] Diego: With Dedicated pinned capacity and tuned batching/kv-caching we can hit that for the interactive model variants. Two caveats: sequence length and model quantization. Longer sequences increase token compute and memory pressure; quantized variants help but there can be small quality delta.
[01:33] Ben: Quick Q: when you say kv cache, do you mean the prefix caching for chat sessions, or the kv of the transformer? We heard a few things in the docs that were a bit fuzzy.
[01:41] Diego: Good callout — we're talking prefix/KV cache at the runtime layer, not a separate database. In practice it keeps hot context in GPU memory to cut recomputation. Sometimes our transcripts show it as K V cache or kee-vee which is why the docs vary.
[01:52] Sam: Ok that matches what our product team thought. Aisha: on security, what do you need from us for SOC2 and SSO?
[01:59] Maya: Short answer: we'll share the SOC2 artifact pack and an access checklist. For SSO we support SAML/Okta and SCIM provisioning. For Private/VPC deployment we provide an on-prem bundle but that elevates the timeline.
[02:13] Aisha: We probably won't do on-prem for this pilot, but VPC with customer-managed KMS is important. Can you confirm Redwood supports CMK integration?
[02:21] Diego: Yes, we support KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys in Private deployments. For hosted pilots we can use envelope encryption and integrate with your KMS via the VPC peering path. There may be a short security review needed.
[02:33] Ben: Another ask: we need token-level cost visibility per route; any chance to get that in the pilot?
[02:39] Maya: Absolutely — Redwood Console already has token-level breakdowns per-route and per-model. For the pilot we'll enable extra ingestion retention for the dashboard so you can slice by user or route.
[02:49] Sam: Nice. About cost — we're trying to compare: hosted with burst vs dedicated reserved. Can you give a ballpark of the monthly delta for our profile?
[02:57] Maya: We can ballpark. For your 1.2k burst and sustained 200-300 rps during peak, dedicated with a medium pool would be roughly 30-40% cheaper per token than pure hosted at scale, but that's assuming you commit to reserved capacity. Hosted with burst avoids commit but could be 20-50% more expensive on peak days. I'll send a scenario spreadsheet.
[03:18] Aisha: That helps. How fast can we pivot to dedicated if the pilot shows it's needed?
[03:22] Diego: From a provisioning perspective we can have dedicated pools online in 2-3 weeks once capacity commit is agreed and provisioning details are shared. There's a short lead-time for GPU allocation but we do autoscale hooks for buffer capacity.
[03:33] Ben: What's the recommended test plan to validate resilience?
[03:36] Diego: Plan: 24h continuous throughput test on staging matching your 99th-percentile traffic, 3 scheduled spike windows (10x baseline) to observe tail latency, and a model fallback test — route to smaller variant when latency or OOM occurs. We'll collect per-token latencies and trace IDs so you can correlate.
[03:52] Aisha: We need to see quality regressions when you move to quantized variants — can you include a small eval run (our eval set of 200 prompts) during the benchmark?
[03:59] Diego: Yes, we can run the eval set at the start and end of the benchmark and report the delta. It will be in the benchmark artifact.
[04:06] Sam: Any gotchas around model caching and cold start? We've seen cold starts inflate latency.
[04:11] Diego: Cold starts can be mitigated with warm pools and prewarmed replicas. Our serving runtime supports continuous batching and warm-hot reuse of KV. For pilot we'll keep a warm buffer during the spike windows. There can still be eviction pressure if you push memory heavy sequences.
[04:25] Ben: On instrumentation, what logs/traces can you provide for us to plug into our APM?
[04:29] Maya: We provide trace hooks and correlation IDs. Diego: We'll include example OpenTelemetry spans and a small README for correlating request IDs to console traces.
[04:38] Aisha: Security doc exchange — timeline? Our security team wants SOC2 report and data flow diagram.
[04:44] Maya: We'll upload the SOC2 package to a secure share once you confirm the security contact. Expect artifacts within 48 hours after we kick off the exchange.
[04:52] Ben: About the pilot gating — what would success look like for Redwood in 30 days?
[04:56] Maya: For us success is: 1) stable P95 below 250ms on interactive routes during peaks you shared, 2) no data exfil >0 incidents, 3) able to route with fallbacks and observe <5% request drop during spikes. If those are met we'll propose rolling pilot to prod with a capacity commit.
[05:12] Aisha: That seems reasonable. We'll add success criteria on our side around user-facing error budget.
[05:17] Sam: Quick question — are there any model variant compatibility issues with your runtime? We use a custom transformer fork with sparse attention.
[05:24] Diego: Sparse attention can be tricky. We can onboard custom ops but we might need a compatibility shim. If you can provide a small snapshot or model proto we can run a compatibility test. That might add a few days to onboarding.
[05:36] Ben: We'll get that to you if it's required. Ok next, can you confirm the benchmarking cadence and what we get as artifacts?
[05:42] Diego: Benchmark cadence: start once Ben and Aisha provide traffic CSV and a model snapshot. We'll run the baseline day + 24h stress test, produce a report with latency histograms, per-token cost estimates, top failure traces, and the eval comparison.
[05:55] Maya: I'll include pricing scenarios in the same email and the pilot SOW template.
[05:59] Aisha: Great. Anything else on the roadmap side of things?
[06:02] Maya: Small note — we're shipping an autoscale smoothing feature in mid-December to reduce tail spikes when bursts ramp quickly. That should help customers with your pattern.
[06:11] Sam: Awesome. That might remove the need for a larger warm buffer.
[06:14] Ben: One more security nit: RBAC at route level — can we restrict embedding generation API to a specific service account?
[06:22] Diego: Yes RBAC is route-level and we can create service-account scoped tokens, and provide audit logs for token usage.
[06:28] Aisha: Perfect. Let's recap next steps and owners.
[06:31] Maya: Recap: Maya will send pilot pricing + SOW + SOC2 pack; Diego will run the benchmark once Ben provides traffic profile and model snapshot; Ben will send traffic CSV and peak windows; Aisha to confirm security contact. We'll aim to have the benchmark started by Dec 3 and a follow-up on week of Dec 7 to review results.
[06:48] Sam: Sounds good.
[06:50] Maya: Any final Qs?
[06:51] Ben: None here.
[06:52] Aisha: No. Thanks all.
[06:54] Maya: Thanks, we'll send notes and artifacts by EOD tomorrow.

End of transcript.
